title: Centered random-variable norm contraction
statement:
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $q\ge2$, and let $c\in[0,1]$. Suppose that for every $z\in\mathbb R$,
\[
|1-cz|^q\le |1+z|^q-q(1+c)z.
\]
If $X\in L^q(\mu)$ has mean zero, then for every $a\in\mathbb R$, the real-valued random-variable norms defined by converting the extended $L^q$ norm to a real number satisfy
\[
N_q(a-cX)\le N_q(a+X).
\]
hypotheses_covered: The scalar inequality holds for every real $z$
replaced: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, $q\ge2$, and $0\le c\le1$ satisfy $|1-cz|^q\le|1+z|^q-q(1+c)z$ for every real $z$. If $X\in L^q(\mu)$ is real with $\int X\,d\mu=0$, then for every $a\in\mathbb R$, $\|a-cX\|_{L^q(\mu)}\le\|a+X\|_{L^q(\mu)}$.
